items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XVI, List of Answers on Topics 14:1
items.html: Although the circles had the power to push them away from the place of the conclusion of the feet of AK — for, by the power of the new center of the second restriction, the place of the conclusion of the feet of AK became more important than the place beneath the Parsa of Nekudim, and therefore they drove them back upward to the place of the Parsa — nevertheless, the circles could not change their order so that they would be arranged exactly like the circles, with Assiyah above and Beriah below. For after all, they themselves came from the vessels of the line [Yosher], and in them operates the matter of up and down, as in the vessels of the line of the TNHY of AK. Therefore, as soon as the vessels returned to their place, the more important [part] among them — the two lower thirds of Tifferet — rose to the more elevated [place], and the most inferior — the vessel of Malchut among them — descended below all of them, in the manner of the vessels of the line. And although, according to the illumination of the Makifim, Malchut, which is Assiyah, is found in a more important place, this does not now come into account at all, for they receive nothing at all from the Makifim, because they are vessels of the line. Thus the circles prevailed over them only to push them away from the place of the conclusion of the feet of AK, back to their place, but they did not prevail over them to reverse the order of the line within them into the order of the circles. (Item 8).
